chunks: Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the resident of Mecca who goes out to his family and then returns to Mecca, with which [type of Hajj] does he enter? He said: 'If his stay in Mecca is more than six months, he does not perform Tamattu', and if it is less than six months, he may perform Tamattu'.'

key_terms.تَمَتُّع: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj with a break)
key_terms.سِتَّةِ أَشْهُرٍ: Six months (the threshold for the ruling)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mecca resident performing Tamattu' Hajj based on the duration of their stay?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between a resident of Mecca (Muqim) and a pilgrim (Ghurab) by using a six-month threshold to determine eligibility for Tamattu' Hajj. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights that prolonged residency transforms one's status, thereby restricting the performance of Tamattu' which is typically reserved for those traveling from outside the Miqat. The narration underscores the importance of intent and duration of stay in defining ritual obligations during the Hajj season.
